T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou r  following:
 ORDER

This common order shall govern disposal of both the appeals as they arise out of a common award arising out of the same accident.
2. M.A.No.2188/2015 has been filed by the owner of the offending vehicle mainly on two grounds i.e. firstly Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and without fitness certificate and secondly the permanent disability assessed and the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
3. M.A.No.104/2015 has been filed by the claimant on the ground of inadequacy of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and seeking enhancement of compensation.
4. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of permanent disability suffered by the claimant the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,90,879/-
in favour of the claimant with interest from filing of the claim petition till its realization.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant in M.A.No.2188/2015 submits that Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions Mohit Guardian Grandmother Kanfulbai vs Suresh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36814079/
2 of the insurance policy and without fitness certificate.

sentences.text: He further submits that as per the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act such requirement is exempted in the case of transport vehicles being run by a local authority or by a person acting under the contract with a local authority and used solely for the purpose of road cleansing, road watering or conservancy purpose.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant opposes the appeal and prays for dismissal of the same.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

Undisputedly, at the time of accident, owner of the offending vehicle had no fitness certificate of the offending vehicle, so it is the duty of the appellant/owner to prove that they are exempted from this requirement but they have unable to adduce any evidence in this regard.
Therefore, Tribunal has rightly held that the owner and driver of the offending vehicle had no fitness certificate at the time of accident.

The coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
vs. Vinod - 2020 Vol.1 MPLJ 142 has held that since the offending vehicle was not having fitness certificate at the time of accident, therefore, terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated, therefore, the insurance company is not jointly and severally liable to make payment of compensation.

vs. Vinod - 2020 Vol.1 MPLJ 142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So the contention of the counsel for the appellant in this regard has no substance.
9. Appellant has filed appeal (MA No.2188/15) on the ground that Tribunal has awarded compensation on the higher side.
The permanent disability assessed by the Tribunal at 60% is also on the higher side.

In support of this contention, he has placed reliance on the order passed by this Court in M.A.No.5604/2022 dated 24.01.2024 (National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Dhyansingh &
others).
10.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Dhyansingh &
others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Perusal of the award passed by the Tribunal it is found that in the present case the left leg of the claimant has been amputated from above the knee.
According to the Workmen's Compensation Act when leg is amputated from the knee, the permanent disability ought to be assessed at 60%.

So considering the evidence adduced before the Tribunal, in the considered opinion of this Court,
Tribunal has rightly assessed the permanent disability at 60% which does not call for any interference by this Court.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the owner (M.A.No.2188/15) fails and is hereby dismissed.
11. M.A No.104/2015 has been filed by the appellant/claimant on the ground that Tribunal has wrongly assessed the amount of compensation which is on the lower side.

12. After hearing counsel for both parties and on perusal of the record it is found that Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,90,879/- in favour of the claimant but in the case of Master Mallikarjun vs.
Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd. - (2014) 14 SCC 396 the apex Court has held that "we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs".

sentences.text:
In the present case, claimant has received 60% permanent disability, so in the light of Mohit Guardian Grandmother Kanfulbai vs Suresh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36814079/

sentences.text: the aforesaid verdict Rs.4 lakhs ought to have been awarded to the claimant with regard to the permanent disability.

In addition to that claimant is entitled to get compensation under the head of discomfort, inconvenience, loss of earning during hospitalization, medical and incidental expenses during hospitalization, future medical expenses for correction of the mal-union of fracture and incidental expenses for such treatment, a further sum of Rs.2,50,000/-.
Thus, the claimant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,50,000/-.
13. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.6,50,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,90,879/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,59,121/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
14. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,59,121/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

15. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.2 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
16. In the result, the appeal (MA No.104/2015) is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
